s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic hypopigmented skin lesions with gradual coalescence and absence of hair growth
salient_findings: Multiple round, hypopigmented macules on face and neck
Lesions symmetrically distributed and ranging from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
Absence of hair growth in affected areas
key_facts: 2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions are asymptomatic
Lesions are round and hypopigmented
Lesions are symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Lesions range from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
No hair growth at site of lesions
Previous treatment for tinea versicolor was unsuccessful
Histopathologic findings show plate-like subepidermal tumor
Neoplastic cords consist of clear/pale epithelial cells with glycogen accumulation
Stroma is formed by fibrous connective tissue
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor

shortlist.label: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis
shortlist.why_kept: Asymptomatic, hypopigmented macules with absence of hair growth match clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Nevus depigmentosus
shortlist.why_kept: Congenital or acquired hypopigmented lesions with sharp borders and absence of hair growth are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Vitiligo
shortlist.why_kept: Hypopigmented macules with sharp borders, although typically associated with hair loss, could be considered in differential

shortlist.label: Pityriasis alba
shortlist.why_kept: Hypopigmented patches with mild scaling, although often associated with atopic dermatitis, could be a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Tuberous sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Hypopigmented macules, known as ash-leaf spots, are a common feature of this genetic disorder

shortlist.label: Nevus of Ito
shortlist.why_kept: Hypopigmented or hyperpigmented macules along the distribution of the posterior supraclavicular and lateral brachial cutaneous nerves could be a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Idiopathic eruptive macular pigmentation
shortlist.why_kept: Asymptomatic, hypopigmented or hyperpigmented macules could be considered, although less common

shortlist.label: Alezzandrini syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral degeneration of the retinal and ipsilateral vitiligo, although rare, could be a possible diagnosis given the unilateral presentation of hypopigmented macules

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on the face and neck, with a 2-year history and absence of symptoms, aligns with the characteristics of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis. The histopathologic findings of a plate-like subepidermal tumor with neoplastic cords consisting of clear/pale epithelial cells and marked elastosis in the dermis surrounding the tumor also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Nevus depigmentosus
rejected.why: Typically presents as a single, well-defined hypopigmented patch, not multiple lesions

rejected.label: Vitiligo
rejected.why: Characterized by complete loss of melanocytes, often with a more rapid progression and potential for widespread involvement

rejected.label: Pityriasis alba
rejected.why: Usually presents with ill-defined, faintly hypopigmented patches and fine scaling, not round, well-defined macules

rejected.label: Tuberous sclerosis
rejected.why: Involves multiple organ systems and is associated with other characteristic skin findings such as angiofibromas and shagreen patches

rejected.label: Nevus of Ito
rejected.why: Typically presents as a congenital or acquired hyperpigmentation in the shoulder region, not hypopigmented macules on the face and neck

rejected.label: Idiopathic eruptive macular pigmentation
rejected.why: Characterized by a sudden onset of multiple, pigmented macules, not hypopigmented

rejected.label: Alezzandrini syndrome
rejected.why: A rare condition involving unilateral degeneration of retinal and ipsilateral vitiligo, not matching the patient's presentation
